analyzed_vuln.description: `output_data()` unconditionally calls `generate_2_noise_channels()` when `s->noise_type == 0`, but only validates `nb_channels == s->max_matrix_channel + 1`. `generate_2_noise_channels()` then writes to `sample_buffer[][max_matrix_channel+1]` and `[][max_matrix_channel+2]`, which can exceed the fixed channel dimension (`int32_t[8]`) when `max_matrix_channel` is already near the limit (e.g., 7), causing out-of-bounds write/read UB (observed index 8). Root cause is missing bounds/consistency validation before enabling 2 extra noise channels.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the TrueHD decode path (`read_access_unit` -> `output_data`), attacker-controlled bitstream fields must set state so that `s->noise_type == 0` and `s->max_matrix_channel` is high enough that adding two synthetic noise channels exceeds `sample_buffer` channel capacity. The existing channel-count check (`nb_channels == max_matrix_channel+1`) still passes, so `output_data` proceeds and `generate_2_noise_channels` indexes past the per-sample channel array.
